title.en: A device maker sees firmware only while a consent grant stands

goal.en: Device self-state facets travel by consent. Derive the device maker's view without a grant, with the household's grant, after the grant is withdrawn, and when another role tries to use the same grant.

note.en: Without consents the maker receives one derived constraint (robot runtime, from the battery facet); the firmware facet is withheld for lack of consent.
The withheld entry names the facet and the reason, so the maker's software can ask the owner for a grant instead of guessing.
With the household's grant cg-maker-1 (scope: the self family, recipient role device_maker, purpose warranty and recalls) the firmware facet is disclosed.

consents.purpose: Warranty support and recall handling for robot neo-1

note.en: The same grant with a withdrawnAt date no longer counts: the facet goes back to withheld.
A grant names its recipient role. Presented for the insurer role, the maker's grant unlocks nothing.

outcome.en: You can design a warranty or recall flow that asks for a ConsentGrant, respects its withdrawal, and never receives the household's other facts. Next: 083 shows the narrowest commercial role, the insurer.
